source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U03: Map guarantee parties,consideration,coextensive liability and contractual limits

payload.title: Read the surety promise before choosing the recovery sequence
payload.core_explanation_md:
A guarantee addresses the principal debtor default through the surety promise to the creditor. Consideration can be the relevant benefit to the principal debtor rather than a separate payment to the surety. The default rule is coextensive liability unless the contract provides otherwise; the undertaking can set limits and conditions.

Do not assume the creditor must always exhaust every remedy against the principal debtor before proceeding against a liable surety. Conversely, a guarantee label does not erase its demand, expiry or scope requirements. An independent bank demand guarantee and an ordinary loan surety file require their actual wording and applicable law; injunction outcomes cannot be predicted from a label alone.

self_check.prompt_text: Must a creditor always exhaust the principal debtor assets first?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Apply the undertaking and applicable liability rule.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A universal exhaustion requirement cannot be assumed.

payload.stem_md: An undertaking expressly caps the surety covered liability. The recovery sheet ignores the cap solely because liability is coextensive by default. What is wrong?

options.text_md: The default rule eliminates every contractual qualification
options.explanation_md: The source expressly recognises contrary provision.

options.text_md: Every cap cancels the guarantee altogether
options.explanation_md: A limit is not necessarily cancellation.

options.text_md: The bank may privately raise the cap after default
The default rule must be read with the contractual limitation
options.explanation_md: Coextensiveness is qualified by the contract.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Coextensiveness is qualified by the contract.
